correctness.rationale: Exact orthonormal basis normalization makes W−sqrt(2)J compact; vanishing-boundary continuous symbols yield compact Bergman Toeplitz operators by Hilbert–Schmidt interior cutoffs; each fixed harmonic monomial Toeplitz matrix converges on its diagonal to a unilateral shift, hence differs by compact operator. The parity decomposition produces a 1×2 Hardy Toeplitz row with symbols a and b; Laurent multiplication gives the upper norm, and weakly-null long plane-wave packets give the matching Calkin lower norm. The antipodal parallelogram identity and continuous approximation prove the exact stated equality, including all quantifiers and boundary cases. The embedded arithmetic checker verifies only exact identities.

value.rationale: Determines the exact norm modulo compacts for every continuous symbol of a natural 2026 Bergman slant operator, not merely qualitative noncompactness. Two independent parity Fourier channels produce an antipodal invariant that distinguishes 1+z and 1+z² and naturally controls perturbations by compacts. The polyphase mechanism is a structural consequence with immediate compactness classification, not an arbitrary numeric specialization.
